These results demonstrate that reciprocity-based compensation can reduce propagation-related bias while preserving local direction-dependent scattering variations, providing a practical signal-normalisation framework for backscatter analysis in heterogeneous anisotropic materials.

AI.tldr: A cross-directional compensation method using reciprocal constraints from opposing inspection surfaces reduces propagation bias in ultrasonic backscatter measurements of heterogeneous anisotropic materials, outperforming conventional attenuation-based compensation.
AI.motivation: In materials with strong anisotropy and spatial heterogeneity, distance-dependent propagation effects obscure genuine microstructural variations in ultrasonic backscatter signals, making interpretation challenging.
AI.method: A cross-directional compensation method that exploits the reciprocal constraint that through-thickness propagation bias contains a shared component between opposing inspection directions; a shared distance-dependent baseline is estimated via anchor-based fitting in the logarithmic amplitude domain and used to compensate measured backscatter profiles.
AI.result: On Ti-6Al-4V samples with macrozones, the method reduced mean standard deviation of directional mismatch from 0.367 to 0.120 and mean absolute fitted gradient from 0.171 to 0.0067, outperforming conventional attenuation compensation.
AI.conclusion: Reciprocity-based compensation effectively reduces propagation-related bias while preserving local direction-dependent scattering variations, offering a practical signal-normalisation framework for backscatter analysis in heterogeneous anisotropic materials.

title: Dynamic electron correlation energy for multireference wavefunction methods from one- and two-electron reduced density matrices
summary: Efficiently recovering dynamic correlation in strongly correlated systems without incurring prohibitive computational costs remains a central challenge in quantum chemistry. In this Perspective, we review and benchmark methods capable of recovering dynamic correlation for multireference wave functions exclusively from low-order reduced density matrices and densities. These approaches require at most the two-electron reduced density matrix of the reference wave function and fall into two categories: density functional theory (DFT)-based methods and purely ab initio multireference adiabatic connection (AC) methods. The former include MC-srDFT, which recovers dynamic correlation through a short-range exchange-correlation functional depending on the charge and spin densities, as well as MC-PDFT and MC-srPDFT, which employ translated functionals that additionally depend on the on-top pair density. Within the post-CASSCF framework, we perform a direct, head-to-head benchmark of these approaches under identical computational settings (including active spaces and basis sets) against challenging multireference problems, including singlet-triplet gaps in organic biradicals, excitation energies, and spin-state splittings in iron complexes. Among the DFT-based methods, MC-srPDFT emerges as the most accurate, underscoring the benefit of incorporating the on-top pair density. However, all considered DFT-based methods fail to provide reliable spin-state energetics for transition-metal complexes. Conversely, linearized AC0 rivals or outperforms more computationally expensive second-order perturbation theory approaches across all benchmark sets. We discuss these findings in the context of alternative formulations and existing literature, highlighting critical limitations and identifying promising directions for the future development of scalable multireference methods.

AI.tldr: This Perspective benchmarks DFT-based (MC-srDFT, MC-PDFT, MC-srPDFT) and ab initio adiabatic connection (AC0) methods that recover dynamic correlation for multireference wave functions using only low-order reduced density matrices. MC-srPDFT is the most accurate among DFT-based methods, but all DFT methods fail for transition-metal spin-state energetics. Linearized AC0 rivals or outperforms second-order perturbation theory across all benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Efficiently recovering dynamic correlation in strongly correlated systems without prohibitive computational costs remains a central challenge in quantum chemistry.
AI.method: Benchmarking DFT-based methods (MC-srDFT, MC-PDFT, MC-srPDFT) and ab initio multireference adiabatic connection (AC0) methods under identical computational settings (active spaces and basis sets) against challenging multireference problems.
AI.result: MC-srPDFT is the most accurate DFT-based method, but all DFT methods fail for transition-metal spin-state energetics. Linearized AC0 rivals or outperforms second-order perturbation theory across all benchmark sets.
AI.conclusion: DFT-based methods incorporating on-top pair density improve accuracy but remain inadequate for transition-metal complexes; AC0 is a promising scalable alternative to perturbative approaches.

title: Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless-type Transition in Site Percolation on the Diamond Hierarchical Lattice
summary: We study site percolation on the diamond hierarchical lattice, a finite-dimensional fractal network, using an exact generating-function analysis. In contrast to bond percolation, site percolation on this lattice does not undergo a transition from a nonpercolating phase to a percolating phase. Instead, the system exhibits a nonpercolating phase for $p<p_{\rm c}$ and a critical phase for $p>p_{\rm c}$. In the critical phase, the size of the largest cluster remains subextensive, scaling as $N^{ψ(p)}$, where the fractal exponent $ψ(p)$ varies continuously with $p$. By analyzing the renormalization-group recursion relation in the vicinity of $p_{\rm c}$, we show that the correlation length exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless-type essential singularity, $ξ(p)\sim \exp \left({\rm const}/\sqrt{p_{\rm c}-p}\right)$ for $p \to p_{\rm c}^-$, which is further confirmed by finite-size scaling analyses showing excellent data collapse. These results demonstrate that critical phases in percolation can emerge even on finite-dimensional networks and that exponential volume growth is not necessary for such phases to appear. We argue that the critical phase on the diamond hierarchical lattice stems from site dilution remaining relevant under renormalization.

AI.tldr: Site percolation on the diamond hierarchical lattice exhibits no standard phase transition; instead it has a nonpercolating phase for p<p_c and a critical phase for p>p_c with subextensive largest clusters and BKT-type essential singularity at p_c.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether critical phases in percolation can emerge on finite-dimensional networks (not requiring exponential volume growth), specifically studying site percolation on the diamond hierarchical lattice.
AI.method: Exact generating-function analysis of site percolation on the diamond hierarchical lattice; renormalization-group recursion relation analysis near p_c; finite-size scaling analyses.
AI.result: No standard percolation transition; a nonpercolating phase (p<p_c) and a critical phase (p>p_c) exist. The largest cluster scales as N^{ψ(p)} with continuously varying fractal exponent. Correlation length shows BKT-type essential singularity ξ(p)~exp(const/√(p_c-p)). Finite-size scaling confirms excellent data collapse.
AI.conclusion: Critical phases in percolation can emerge on finite-dimensional networks, and exponential volume growth is not required. The critical phase arises because site dilution remains relevant under renormalization.

title: Anomalous acoustoelectric signatures of chiral superconductivity
summary: The identification of unconventional pairing in two-dimensional materials is a central challenge in modern condensed matter physics. While chiral p-wave superconductivity offers a promising platform for topological quantum computing, its detection remains elusive due to the inherent limitations of optical probes in the two-dimensional limit. We propose the anomalous acoustoelectric effect as a robust, alternative to optical signature of p-wave paring symmetry. We demonstrate that an acoustic wave induces a transverse dc current resulting in a measurable condensate phase difference on sample boundaries originating from the anisotropic scattering of quasiparticles in the absence of an external magnetic field. Crucially, the quasiparticle-mediated acoustoelectric response dominates near the critical temperature and, unlike the superconducting condensate, is not suppressed by electron-hole asymmetry factor. These results establish the anomalous acoustoelectric effect as a high-sensitivity electrical probe of the chiral order parameter, providing a tool for experimental detecting of unconventional pairing in superconductors.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using the anomalous acoustoelectric effect as a sensitive electrical probe to detect chiral p-wave superconductivity in two-dimensional materials, overcoming limitations of optical methods.
AI.motivation: Detecting unconventional chiral p-wave pairing in 2D materials is challenging because optical probes are limited in the 2D limit, yet such pairing is crucial for topological quantum computing.
AI.method: The authors theoretically demonstrate that an acoustic wave induces a transverse dc current via anisotropic quasiparticle scattering, producing a measurable condensate phase difference at sample boundaries without an external magnetic field.
AI.result: The quasiparticle-mediated acoustoelectric response dominates near Tc and is not suppressed by the electron-hole asymmetry factor, unlike the superconducting condensate response.
AI.conclusion: The anomalous acoustoelectric effect serves as a high-sensitivity electrical probe for chiral order parameters, offering a practical experimental tool for detecting unconventional pairing in superconductors.

title: Spin Glass Mapping of the Parallel Minority Game
summary: The parallel minority game (PMG) extends the classical minority game to many choices, with each agent restricted to two predetermined alternatives. In this condition, minimizing the population variance across all choices is a complex combinatorial optimization problem. We show that this minimization is exactly equivalent to finding the ground state of an Ising spin glass in the mean-field limit, i.e., the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. By encoding the agent choices as spin variables, the variance becomes a quadratic Hamiltonian with quenched random couplings $J_{ij}$ and random fields $h_i$. This mapping reveals inherent frustration and connects the PMG to the well developed theory of spin glasses, providing a new perspective on the frozen, sub-optimal configurations observed in stochastic strategies.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that minimizing population variance in the parallel minority game (PMG) with many choices is equivalent to finding the ground state of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Ising spin glass model, mapping agent choices to spin variables and variance to a quadratic Hamiltonian with random couplings and fields.
AI.motivation: To understand why stochastic strategies in the parallel minority game lead to frozen, sub-optimal configurations, by connecting the PMG's variance minimization problem to the well-studied theory of spin glasses.
AI.method: The authors encode agent choices as Ising spin variables and show that the population variance across all choices maps exactly to a quadratic Hamiltonian with quenched random couplings $J_{ij}$ and random fields $h_i$, equivalent to the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick mean-field spin glass model.
AI.result: The variance minimization in the parallel minority game is exactly equivalent to finding the ground state of an Ising spin glass in the mean-field limit (Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model), revealing inherent frustration in the system.
AI.conclusion: This mapping provides a new perspective on the frozen, sub-optimal configurations observed in stochastic strategies of the PMG by connecting it to the established theory of spin glasses.

title: Direct observation of the transverse near field of an edge excitation and associated slow secondary dynamics in a fractional quantum Hall state
summary: We report stroboscopic time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) microscopy and spectroscopy revealing the transverse near field of an edge excitation in a $ν=1/3$ fractional quantum Hall (FQH) state. Time-resolved $y$-$t$ maps reveal an immediate PL response extending more than $30~μ\mathrm{m}$ into the bulk transverse to the edge when the edge magnetoplasmon (EMP) passes the mesa boundary. The nearly instantaneous nature of this long-range response identifies it as the non-radiative, quasi-electrostatic near field, revealing the EMP as a spatially extended collective excitation rather than a strictly one-dimensional charge-density oscillation. We also observe secondary bulk-side responses distinct from the immediate transverse near-field response. The coexistence of these immediate and secondary responses shows that electrically launched edge excitations produce bulk-side dynamics on widely separated time scales.

AI.tldr: Stroboscopic time-resolved PL microscopy reveals that edge magnetoplasmons in a ν=1/3 FQH state generate an instantaneous, long-range (~30 μm) transverse near-field response in the bulk, identifying EMPs as spatially extended collective excitations, alongside secondary bulk-side dynamics on separated time scales.
AI.motivation: To understand the spatial extent and bulk coupling of edge magnetoplasmons in fractional quantum Hall states, challenging the assumption that EMPs are strictly one-dimensional edge excitations.
AI.method: Stroboscopic time-resolved photoluminescence microscopy and spectroscopy, capturing y-t maps of the transverse near field from an edge excitation in a ν=1/3 FQH state.
AI.result: An immediate PL response extending >30 μm into the bulk transverse to the edge upon EMP passage, plus secondary bulk-side responses on different time scales.
AI.conclusion: EMPs are spatially extended collective excitations with non-radiative quasi-electrostatic near fields that couple into the bulk, and edge excitations produce bulk dynamics on widely separated time scales.

title: Enhancement in Magnetic and Magnetocaloric Properties of CoFe2O4 Nanofibers at Lower Temperatures
summary: This research paper investigates new and first insights into the magnetic and magnetocaloric properties of one-dimensional (1D) cobalt ferrite CoFe2O4 (CFO) nanofibers elaborated by sol gel based electrospinning technique, particularly focusing on their behavior at low temperatures for specific applications. The calcined CFO nanofibers microstructural, structural, magnetic, and magnetocaloric properties were explored. The nanofibers (NFs) microstructure, with an average diameter of 210 nm, was examined by scanning and transmission electron microscopies (SEM, TEM). The X-ray diffraction (XRD) of the CFO nanofibers showed a pure cubic close-packed (c.c.p) spinel crystalline structure with the F d 3 -m space group. The Raman spectroscopic studies further confirm the cubic inverse spinel phase. The Magnetic properties were explored as a function of temperature, ranging from 10 to 300 K, a ferromagnetic behaviour was observed with the highest saturation magnetization of 75.87 emu g(-1) and a coercivity of 723 Oe at room temperature. The variation of the magnetic entropy was measured indirectly using the Maxwell approach with an increasing magnetic field. A maximum of Delta(S)=1.71 J K-1 was reached around 32 K. At 180 K, the associated adiabatic temperature change, Delta (Tmax), was 0.93 K, with a large RCP value of 7.58 J kg-1 was measured, which is reasonably high for the corresponding nanoparticles (NPs). This work may suggest that 1D CFO nanofibers offer a promising route for the production of nanostructured magnetic materials, potentially impacting various electronic and electromagnetic device applications at low temperatures.

AI.tldr: This study explores the magnetic and magnetocaloric properties of 1D CoFe2O4 nanofibers (210 nm diameter) fabricated via sol-gel electrospinning, revealing ferromagnetic behavior at 10–300 K with high saturation magnetization (75.87 emu/g), a maximum magnetic entropy change of 1.71 J/K at 32 K, adiabatic temperature change of 0.93 K at 180 K, and an RCP of 7.58 J/kg, suggesting promise for low-temperature electronic and electromagnetic devices.
AI.motivation: To investigate new insights into the magnetic and magnetocaloric properties of one-dimensional cobalt ferrite nanofibers, particularly at low temperatures, for potential use in electronic and electromagnetic device applications.
AI.method: CFO nanofibers were fabricated using sol-gel based electrospinning, followed by calcination. Characterization included SEM, TEM for microstructure; XRD and Raman spectroscopy for structural/phase analysis; and magnetic measurements (10–300 K) with magnetocaloric properties assessed via the Maxwell approach for magnetic entropy change.
AI.result: Pure cubic inverse spinel phase confirmed. Ferromagnetic behavior with Ms = 75.87 emu/g and Hc = 723 Oe at RT. Maximum ΔS = 1.71 J/K at 32 K, ΔTmax = 0.93 K at 180 K, RCP = 7.58 J/kg.
AI.conclusion: 1D CFO nanofibers fabricated via electrospinning demonstrate promising magnetocaloric properties at low temperatures, offering a viable route for nanostructured magnetic materials in low-temperature electronic and electromagnetic device applications.

title: Simultaneously monitoring Ga adsorption and desorption kinetics on GaN(0001) using four in situ techniques
summary: We present a systematic investigation of Ga adsorption and desorption kinetics on the wurtzite GaN(0001) surface using four in situ techniques operated simultaneously: reflection high-energy electron diffraction, laser reflectometry, line-of-sight quadrupole mass spectrometry, and optical pyrometry. Flux- and temperature-dependent experiments are performed for Ga coverages ranging from the submonolayer to the droplet regime. Despite their distinct transient responses, the signals from all four techniques and their trends with surface coverage are quantitatively reproduced by a unified kinetic model of Ga adsorption, diffusion, and desorption. An Arrhenius analysis of the Ga adlayer desorption yields an activation energy of (2.87 $\pm$ 0.04) eV.

AI.tldr: A systematic investigation of Ga adsorption/desorption kinetics on GaN(0001) using four in situ techniques is presented, with all signals quantitatively reproduced by a unified kinetic model, yielding a desorption activation energy of 2.87 ± 0.04 eV.
AI.motivation: To understand and quantitatively model Ga adsorption and desorption kinetics on wurtzite GaN(0001) surfaces across a wide coverage range (submonolayer to droplet regime) using multiple complementary in situ characterization techniques.
AI.method: Four simultaneous in situ techniques (RHEED, laser reflectometry, line-of-sight QMS, and optical pyrometry) were used to study Ga adsorption/desorption on GaN(0001). Flux- and temperature-dependent experiments were conducted from submonolayer to droplet coverages. A unified kinetic model incorporating Ga adsorption, diffusion, and desorption was developed to reproduce all signals quantitatively.
AI.result: All four techniques' distinct transient responses and coverage trends were quantitatively reproduced by the unified kinetic model. Arrhenius analysis of Ga adlayer desorption gave an activation energy of 2.87 ± 0.04 eV.
AI.conclusion: The study achieves a comprehensive, quantitative understanding of Ga surface kinetics on GaN(0001) validated by four independent in situ techniques, providing a reliable activation energy value for Ga desorption.

title: pANO-F12: An atomic natural orbital-inspired route to more compact basis sets for F12 explicitly correlated methods
comment: 33 pages draft; basis sets part of download package
summary: Explicitly correlated methods such as MP2-F12 and CCSD(F12*) exhibit much faster basis set convergence (asymptotically $\propto L^{-7}$, with L the highest angular momentum) than orbital-only approaches. Yet it has been pointed out that cc-pVnZ-F12 basis sets themselves are substantially larger than the corresponding cc-pVnZ, and specifically that cc-pVDZ-F12 is the size of cc-pVTZ. One way to generate compact basis sets in an orbital-only context are Atomic Natural Orbital (ANO) basis sets [J. Almlöf and P. R. Taylor, JCP 86, 4070 (1987)]. However, obtaining the required first-order reduced density matrix while properly accounting for the F12 geminal is problematic. In this work, we show that an energy minimization-based contraction process under linear independence constraints yields `pseudo-ANO' (pANO) basis sets that are functionally equivalent in quality. Subsequently, we apply this recipe to obtain pANO-F12 basis sets from the same elements, then validate them for several thermochemical benchmarks and for the hypersensitive out-of-plane vibrations of benzene. We show that, unlike cc-pVnZ-F12, pANO-F12 exhibits the familiar shell structure seen in cc-pVnZ and ANO basis sets, and that pANO-F12 offers a route to more compact F12 basis sets more amenable to medium-sized systems, especially in conjunction with localized pair natural orbital approaches. Overall, the pANO approach is most beneficial for the smaller double-and triple-zeta basis sets, offering either superior performance to cc-pVnZ-F12 at same cost, or similar performance at lower cost.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces pANO-F12 basis sets—compact, energy-minimized contractions under linear independence constraints—that achieve functional equivalence to ANO basis sets while enabling faster MP2-F12/CCSD(F12*) convergence with a familiar shell structure, outperforming or matching cc-pVnZ-F12 at lower cost, especially for double- and triple-zeta levels.
AI.motivation: Standard cc-pVnZ-F12 basis sets are substantially larger than cc-pVnZ (e.g., cc-pVDZ-F12 ≈ cc-pVTZ size), limiting applicability to medium-sized systems. ANO basis sets offer compactness in orbital-only contexts, but constructing them while properly accounting for F12 geminal correlation is problematic.
AI.method: The authors perform energy minimization-based contraction under linear independence constraints to generate "pseudo-ANO" (pANO) basis sets, then extend this recipe to create pANO-F12 basis sets. These are validated against thermochemical benchmarks and benzene out-of-plane vibrations.
AI.result: pANO-F12 basis sets exhibit the familiar shell structure of cc-pVnZ and ANO (unlike cc-pVnZ-F12). They offer superior performance at the same cost or similar performance at lower cost. The approach is most beneficial at double- and triple-zeta levels and is well-suited for localized pair natural orbital methods.
AI.conclusion: pANO-F12 provides a route to more compact F12 basis sets that are more tractable for medium-sized systems, bridging the gap between compactness and explicit correlation accuracy.

title: Aggregation-Fragmentation Processes with Broken Detailed Balance
summary: We study aggregation-fragmentation processes in which pairs of clusters can aggregate, and each cluster can break into two fragments. If the rates of aggregation and fragmentation do not depend on the masses, detailed balance does not hold, but nonequilibrium steady states can still be deduced from an exact solution for the Laplace transform. For models in which aggregation rates remain constant but fragmentation rates scale as $(\text{mass})^β$, detailed balance holds only when $β=1$. Away from this solvable case, we employ asymptotic techniques and show that when $β\geq 0$, the steady states share similarities with those from the mass-independent ($β=0$) model. An instantaneous shattering transition with continuous mass loss occurs when $β<0$.

AI.tldr: The paper studies aggregation-fragmentation processes with constant aggregation rates and fragmentation rates scaling as (mass)^β. Exact solutions via Laplace transform reveal detailed balance only at β=1. For β≥0, steady states resemble the mass-independent (β=0) case; for β<0, an instantaneous shattering transition with continuous mass loss occurs.
AI.motivation: To understand nonequilibrium steady states in aggregation-fragmentation processes where detailed balance does not hold, particularly when aggregation and fragmentation rates depend differently on mass.
AI.method: Exact solution via Laplace transform for the mass-independent case; asymptotic techniques for the β-dependent scaling regime.
AI.result: Detailed balance holds only when β=1. For β≥0, steady states resemble the mass-independent model. For β<0, an instantaneous shattering transition with continuous mass loss occurs.
AI.conclusion: Nonequilibrium steady states can be deduced even without detailed balance, with distinct phase behavior depending on the scaling exponent β.

title: Superconductivity in doped spin multimer systems
summary: Binding energy, which quantifies pair formation, is a key factor in the emergence of superconductivity. Here, we show that even when multiple spins are complexly coupled, hole-doped systems, which can be mapped onto the universal hardcore boson model in the strong-binding-energy limit, exhibit promising signatures of superconductivity. We analytically and numerically demonstrate this concept in the double Kondo lattice model. Using the density-matrix renormalization group method, we show that a pairing state is maintained via a crossover even for parameters away from the strong-coupling regime. Additionally, we find that once binding energies are sufficiently generated, pair correlations develop similarly regardless of the details of local spin correlations. Our findings suggest useful guidelines for research on superconductivity.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that hole-doped systems with complex spin couplings, mappable to a universal hardcore boson model in the strong-binding limit, show promising superconductivity signatures, as shown analytically and numerically in the double Kondo lattice model using DMRG. Pairing persists via crossover away from strong coupling, and pair correlations develop similarly once binding energies are sufficient, offering guidelines for superconductivity research.
AI.motivation: To understand how binding energy, as a key factor for pair formation, drives superconductivity in systems with complex spin couplings, and to identify universal conditions for superconductivity beyond the strong-coupling regime.
AI.method: Analytical mapping to the universal hardcore boson model in the strong-binding-energy limit; numerical density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method applied to the double Kondo lattice model.
AI.result: Pairing state is maintained via a crossover for parameters away from the strong-coupling regime; pair correlations develop similarly once binding energies are sufficiently generated, regardless of local spin correlation details.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest useful guidelines for research on superconductivity, indicating that sufficient binding energy, not the specifics of spin correlations, is the key driver for pairing.

title: Gyromagnetic Quantum Friction in Rayleigh Vorticity Baths
summary: We identify an intrinsic zero-temperature relaxation channel for near-surface spins gyromagnetically coupled to Rayleigh-wave vorticity. This surface-mode contribution requires no thermal phonons, unlike Raman relaxation, and is fixed by Rayleigh vorticity rather than material-specific $g$-factor modulation. The Rayleigh-vorticity bath is super-Ohmic and evanescent with depth, producing field and depth scalings of spin relaxation. These scalings establish shallow spin sensors and hybrid surface-acoustic-wave spin interfaces as detectors of Rayleigh-wave acoustic quantum friction in solids.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies a zero-temperature relaxation mechanism for near-surface spins coupled to Rayleigh-wave vorticity, producing super-Ohmic, evanescent relaxation with distinct depth and field scalings, enabling detection of acoustic quantum friction via spin sensors and hybrid surface-acoustic-wave interfaces.
AI.motivation: To uncover an intrinsic, thermally independent relaxation pathway for near-surface spins that arises from gyromagnetic coupling to Rayleigh-wave vorticity, offering a mechanism distinct from conventional Raman relaxation.
AI.method: The authors theoretically analyze the coupling between near-surface spins and the vorticity field of Rayleigh surface acoustic waves, deriving the relaxation rates and characterizing the spectral density as super-Ohmic and depth-evanescent.
AI.result: The Rayleigh-vorticity bath is super-Ohmic and evanescent with depth, yielding specific field and depth scalings for spin relaxation. The mechanism requires no thermal phonons and is independent of material-specific g-factor modulation.
AI.conclusion: Shallow spin sensors and hybrid surface-acoustic-wave spin interfaces can serve as detectors of Rayleigh-wave acoustic quantum friction in solids.

title: Conductivity of a Non-Galilean--Invariant Fermi Liquid: Exact Solution of the Kinetic Equation
summary:
We obtain an exact expression for the conductivity of a disordered,
  non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid by solving the kinetic equation with both screened Coulomb and $z=3$ Pomeranchuk critical interactions. While consistent with previous asymptotic results, our solution shows that electron-electron interactions enter the conductivity solely via the quasiparticle scattering time, $τ_\mathrm{ee}$. Accordingly, the crossovers between the collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes occur when $1/τ_\mathrm{ee}$ becomes comparable to the larger of the impurity scattering rate and the probe frequency, $Ω$. In addition, the exact solution yields the optical response in the hydrodynamic regime, $Ω\ll 1/τ_\mathrm{ee}$, which is inaccessible within perturbation theory. Near a $z=3$ Pomeranchuk quantum critical point, consistency between the kinetic-equation and Kubo approaches requires proper inclusion of mass renormalization within the Eliashberg approximation, which also ensures that the crossover between the collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes in the optical conductivity occurs at the Planckian scale $Ω\sim T$.

AI.tldr: The paper derives an exact expression for conductivity of a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid by solving the kinetic equation with screened Coulomb and z=3 Pomeranchuk critical interactions. Electron-electron interactions enter conductivity solely via quasiparticle scattering time τ_ee. Crossovers between collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes occur when 1/τ_ee matches the larger of impurity scattering rate or probe frequency Ω. Near a z=3 Pomeranchuk quantum critical point, consistency between kinetic-equation and Kubo approaches requires proper mass renormalization within the Eliashberg approximation, ensuring the crossover occurs at the Planckian scale Ω ∼ T.
AI.motivation: To obtain an exact expression for the conductivity of a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid by solving the kinetic equation with screened Coulomb and z=3 Pomeranchuk critical interactions.
AI.method: Solving the kinetic equation with both screened Coulomb and z=3 Pomeranchuk critical interactions, and using the Eliashberg approximation for mass renormalization.
AI.result: Electron-electron interactions enter conductivity solely via τ_ee; crossovers occur when 1/τ_ee becomes comparable to the larger of impurity scattering rate and Ω; consistency between kinetic-equation and Kubo approaches requires mass renormalization within the Eliashberg approximation.
AI.conclusion: Near a z=3 Pomeranchuk quantum critical point, the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes in optical conductivity occurs at the Planckian scale Ω ∼ T.

title: Uncovering Antipolar Ordering and Pressure-Tunable Phases in Hexagonal LaN
summary: We predict an antipolar instability in hexagonal LaN using first-principles density functional theory. Starting from a nonpolar hexagonal phase, we identify competing polar and antipolar zone-center phonon instabilities. Condensation of the polar and antipolar modes stabilizes, respectively, dynamically stable wurtzite (WZ) phase and an hexagonal antipolar (AP) phase which is characterized by alternating local polarization and zero net macroscopic polarization within the unit cell. At ambient conditions, the AP phase is metastable with respect to the WZ phase, and a finite energy barrier exists between these phases, suggesting a possible polarization-switching pathway via the AP intermediate state. The energy barrier between the WZ and AP phases decreases with increasing pressure, indicating enhanced tunability between polar and antipolar states. The sublattice polarization increases with pressure in the AP phase, while it decreases in the WZ phase. We further find that, with increasing pressure, the rock-salt and tetragonal phases of LaN become more stable than the hexagonal phases (AP and WZ). Consequently, the realization of the AP phase is more favorable in the low-pressure regime, where hexagonal phases remain energetically competitive. These results demonstrate pressure-driven competition between polar and antipolar phases in LaN and point toward antiferroelectric-like behavior in this binary nitride system.

AI.tldr: First-principles calculations predict an antipolar (AP) phase in hexagonal LaN driven by competing polar and antipolar phonon instabilities. The AP phase is metastable relative to the wurtzite (WZ) phase at ambient conditions, with a pressure-tunable energy barrier between them. Sublattice polarization shows opposite pressure dependence in the two phases. At high pressure, rock-salt and tetragonal phases become more stable, making the AP phase favorable only at low pressure. This suggests antiferroelectric-like behavior in LaN.
AI.motivation: To predict and characterize an antipolar instability in hexagonal LaN using first-principles density functional theory, exploring the competition between polar and antipolar phases and their pressure-dependent behavior.
AI.method: First-principles density functional theory calculations analyzing zone-center phonon instabilities, phase stability comparisons, and pressure-dependent energy barriers between polar (wurtzite) and antipolar (AP) phases.
AI.result: The AP phase is metastable with respect to the WZ phase at ambient conditions; a finite energy barrier exists between them. The barrier decreases with increasing pressure. Sublattice polarization increases with pressure in the AP phase but decreases in the WZ phase. At high pressure, rock-salt and tetragonal phases become more stable than hexagonal phases.
AI.conclusion: Pressure-driven competition between polar and antipolar phases in LaN suggests antiferroelectric-like behavior in this binary nitride system, with the AP phase being more favorable in the low-pressure regime.

title: A Solid-state Sub-nm Pore for Single-mer Resolution Sequencing
summary: Nanopore sequencing accuracy is inherently limited by the quality of data from individual molecular translocation events, requiring advances beyond traditional sequencing-by-synthesis methods. We introduce an oxidized pyramidal sub-nm pore (OPSP) integrated in a threeterminal sensing platform, where the sub-nm silicon pore functions as an electrode for detecting displacement currents across an oxide barrier, induced by counter-ion migration within the electric double layer. This platform achieves sub-1-nm-scale spatial resolution and a signal-tonoise ratio (SNR) up to 15 for biopolymer sequencing, enabling direct identification of individual bases in single-stranded DNA and single amino acids in peptides, with raw-read accuracies exceeding 98.5% and 95.5%, respectively, without consensus-based computational correction. The OPSP demonstrates high acid tolerance, reusability in varied chemical environments, and operational stability for over six months. This work establishes OPSP as a durable, high-accuracy platform for single-mer resolution sequencing, defining a reliable and robust paradigm for next-generation sequencing technologies.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an oxidized pyramidal sub-nm pore (OPSP) integrated in a three-terminal sensing platform that uses displacement current detection for direct, single-molecule biopolymer sequencing, achieving >98.5% accuracy for DNA and >95.5% for peptides without consensus correction, with sub-1-nm spatial resolution, SNR up to 15, and over six months of operational stability.
AI.motivation: Nanopore sequencing accuracy is limited by the quality of data from individual molecular translocation events, requiring advances beyond traditional sequencing-by-synthesis methods.
AI.method: An oxidized pyramidal sub-nm pore (OPSP) integrated in a three-terminal sensing platform, where a sub-nm silicon pore functions as an electrode to detect displacement currents across an oxide barrier induced by counter-ion migration within the electric double layer.
AI.result: Achieves sub-1-nm-scale spatial resolution and SNR up to 15; raw-read accuracies >98.5% for ssDNA and >95.5% for peptides without consensus correction; high acid tolerance, reusability, and >6-month operational stability.
AI.conclusion: OPSP is a durable, high-accuracy platform for single-mer resolution sequencing, establishing a reliable and robust paradigm for next-generation sequencing technologies.

title: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: Advancing Open-Source Software for Efficient and Scalable Molecular Simulation
summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) enable atomistic simulations with near ab initio accuracy at significantly reduced computational cost, but their broader adoption is often limited by fragmented tooling, limited scalability, and inflexible software design. We present mlip v2, a new generation of the mlip library that advances efficient and scalable molecular simulation through a unified and extensible framework. The new release features a targeted API redesign with improved modularity and control, enabling flexible customization of training, data processing, and simulation workflows. It further integrates a new high-performance backend for equivariant operations, e3j, significantly accelerating model inference and simulations. In addition, the framework introduces a range of entirely new capabilities, including the eSEN architecture with a Mixture-of-Experts formulation for scalable training on large and diverse datasets, improved handling of electrostatics through more physically grounded charge modeling and long-range interaction treatment, and advanced simulation features such as NPT ensembles and nudged elastic band methods. Together, these extensions significantly broaden the scope of MLIP applications, enabling efficient modeling of complex, reactive, and out-of-equilibrium systems, and bridging the gap between ML research and practical molecular simulation applications. The library is available on GitHub and on PyPI under the Apache license 2.0.

AI.tldr: mlip v2 is a redesigned machine learning interatomic potentials library with improved modularity, a high-performance equivariant backend (e3j), new architectures (eSEN with Mixture-of-Experts), enhanced electrostatics modeling, and advanced simulation features (NPT, NEB), aiming to bridge ML research and practical molecular simulation.
AI.motivation: Broader adoption of MLIPs is limited by fragmented tooling, limited scalability, and inflexible software design; mlip v2 addresses these issues through a unified and extensible framework.
AI.method: The library features an API redesign for modularity and control, integration of the e3j high-performance backend for equivariant operations, the eSEN architecture with Mixture-of-Experts for scalable training, improved charge modeling and long-range electrostatics, and support for NPT ensembles and nudged elastic band methods.
AI.result: Significantly accelerated model inference and simulations, scalable training on large and diverse datasets, more physically grounded charge modeling, and broader applicability to complex, reactive, and out-of-equilibrium systems.
AI.conclusion: mlip v2 broadens the scope of MLIP applications and bridges the gap between ML research and practical molecular simulation; the library is publicly available on GitHub and PyPI under Apache 2.0.

title: The cell fluid model with Curie-Weiss interactions: special cases and analytical results
summary: Inspired by previous extensive numerical studies of a cell fluid model with Curie-Weiss interactions, we concentrate on some analytically tractable special cases in its description. The key ingredient of the model is a competition between global attraction and local repulsion interactions between particles with coupling constants $J_1$ and $J_2$, respectively. We provide analytical results in several limiting cases, including the ideal-gas limit $J_1=J_2=0$ and the strong-repulsion limit $J_2\gg J_1$. For $J_2\gg J_1$, a detailed analytical study is presented. We derive explicit expressions for the critical point parameters, the equation of state, and the binodal and spinodal curves in closed form. The equation of state is found to be in full agreement with that of the van der Waals lattice gas, and the order parameter satisfies the standard Curie-Weiss equation. In a neighborhood of the critical point, a Landau expansion is shown to have the same form and symmetry as that of the classical lattice gas within the mean-field approximation. Moreover, based on the explicit knowledge of a few leading terms in the asymptotic expansion of the deformed exponential function governing the physics of the cell model, we extend its validity range to include the marginal case of thermodynamic stability, $J_1=J_2$. In particular, this extension makes a consideration of the ideal-gas limit $J_1=J_2=0$ formally legitimate. For the generic marginal case $J_1=J_2\ne0$ systematically avoided in previous works, we present numerical data and phase diagrams that augment their findings for $J_2>J_1$.

AI.tldr: The paper analytically studies a cell fluid model with competing global attraction ($J_1$) and local repulsion ($J_2$), deriving exact results in limiting cases (ideal-gas, strong-repulsion, and marginal $J_1=J_2$), showing equivalence to van der Waals lattice gas and Curie-Weiss behavior near criticality.
AI.motivation: To provide analytical tractability for a cell fluid model with Curie-Weiss interactions, where previous work was largely numerical, by solving special limiting cases and extending the validity to the previously avoided marginal case $J_1=J_2$.
AI.method: Analytical derivation in limiting cases: ideal-gas limit ($J_1=J_2=0$), strong-repulsion limit ($J_2\gg J_1$), and marginal case ($J_1=J_2\neq0$). Landau expansion near criticality. Asymptotic expansion of deformed exponential function to extend validity.
AI.result: Explicit closed-form expressions for critical point parameters, equation of state (matching van der Waals lattice gas), binodal/spinodal curves. Order parameter follows Curie-Weiss equation. Landau expansion matches classical lattice gas in mean-field. Extension to $J_1=J_2$ renders the ideal-gas limit formally legitimate. Numerical phase diagrams for the marginal case.
AI.conclusion: The model with competing attractions and repulsions is analytically solvable in several limits, reproduces known mean-field results, and can be extended to the marginal stability case $J_1=J_2$ which was previously avoided.

title: Fabrication and transfer of ultra-thin YBa$2$Cu$3$O$_{7-x}$ film on SrTiO$_3$ nanomembrane
summary: The fabrication of free-standing ultra-thin films from high-temperature (high-Tc) superconductors is of great interest for the development of superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors with high operating temperatures. We successfully fabricate a millimeter-sized, high-quality, ultra-thin YBa$2$Cu$3$O$_{7-x}$ (YBCO) film on an SrTiO$_3$/Sr$_{1.5}$Ca$_{1.5}$Al$_2$O$_6$ (STO/SCAO) bilayer using high-pressure sputtering. The STO nanomembranes with the YBCO films are released by dissolving the water-soluble SCAO sacrificial layer and transferred onto the SiO2/Si substrate. X-ray diffraction confirms that STO and YBCO crystallinity is preserved following transfer onto SiO2/Si substrates. Microbridges patterned from the transferred YBCO films exhibit a critical temperature of 88.8 K and a critical current density of 6.8 MA/cm2 at 77 K, demonstrating robust superconducting transport after transfer. The thermal boundary conductance across the van der Waals interface between the STO nanomembrane with YBCO film and the SiO2/Si substrate, measured over 15-75 K, is significantly reduced compared to that of epitaxial YBCO film on bulk STO leading to modified energy relaxation and enhanced stability of transient resistive states. These results establish ultra-thin YBCO films on optically transparent STO nanomembranes as a platform for integrating high-Tc superconducting devices with SiO2/Si-based photonic structures.

AI.tldr: Researchers fabricated millimeter-sized ultra-thin YBCO films on STO nanomembranes using a water-soluble SCAO sacrificial layer, achieving high critical temperature (88.8 K) and current density (6.8 MA/cm² at 77 K), with reduced thermal boundary conductance that enhances stability for superconducting detector applications on SiO₂/Si substrates.
AI.motivation: To develop free-standing ultra-thin high-Tc superconducting films for enabling superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) that can operate at higher temperatures, addressing the need for integrating high-Tc superconductors with silicon-based photonic platforms.
AI.method: High-pressure sputtering was used to deposit YBCO on STO/SCAO bilayer; water-soluble SCAO served as a sacrificial layer to release STO nanomembranes with YBCO films, which were then transferred onto SiO₂/Si substrates. Structural and transport properties were characterized via XRD, critical temperature, critical current density, and thermal boundary conductance measurements.
AI.result: YBCO films preserved crystallinity after transfer, exhibited Tc = 88.8 K and Jc = 6.8 MA/cm² at 77 K. Thermal boundary conductance across the van der Waals interface was significantly reduced compared to epitaxial YBCO on bulk STO, leading to modified energy relaxation and enhanced stability of transient resistive states.
AI.conclusion: Ultra-thin YBCO films on optically transparent STO nanomembranes provide a viable platform for integrating high-Tc superconducting devices with SiO₂/Si-based photonic structures, advancing the prospect of high-operating-temperature SNSPDs.

title: Quasinormal mode quantization of bound and propagating photons in complex lightguiding nanostructures for integrated devices
summary: Open optical or plasmonic resonators are placed on and connected through surfaces or via waveguides, forming complex lightguiding nanostructures, e.g. for integrated photonic quantum devices. We derive general boundary conditions for quasinormal modes that account for the structure's specific geometry. We then present a general quantization scheme for multiple, interacting quasinormal-mode cavities coupled to quantum emitters and to a non-bosonic bath of propagating photons on waveguides or a surface. We derive a system-bath Hamiltonian with rigorously defined coupling elements that can be computed using Maxwell solvers, including light-matter coupling between the electromagnetic field and quantum emitters. We define system-bath correlation functions for an effective, bath-mediated, and time-delayed interaction between the quasinormal modes and quantum emitters, which is a main ingredient commonly used to simulate open quantum system dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper derives general boundary conditions for quasinormal modes in open optical/plasmonic resonators and presents a quantization scheme for multiple interacting cavities coupled to quantum emitters and a non-bosonic photon bath, yielding a system-bath Hamiltonian with computable coupling elements and bath-mediated correlation functions for simulating open quantum system dynamics.
AI.motivation: To provide rigorous boundary conditions and a quantization framework for quasinormal modes in complex lightguiding nanostructures (e.g., integrated photonic quantum devices), enabling accurate modeling of coupled resonator-emitter systems interacting with propagating photon baths on surfaces or waveguides.
AI.method: Derivation of general boundary conditions for quasinormal modes based on specific geometry; formulation of a quantization scheme for multiple interacting quasinormal-mode cavities coupled to quantum emitters and a non-bosonic propagating-photon bath; derivation of a system-bath Hamiltonian with coupling elements computable via Maxwell solvers; definition of system-bath correlation functions for effective bath-mediated time-delayed interactions.
AI.result: A general quantization scheme with rigorously defined coupling elements, a system-bath Hamiltonian, and bath-mediated correlation functions that enable simulation of open quantum system dynamics for coupled quasinormal-mode cavities and quantum emitters.
AI.conclusion: The derived framework provides a computationally tractable approach to model open quantum system dynamics in integrated photonic nanostructures, with coupling parameters obtainable from standard Maxwell solvers and effective time-delayed interactions captured via system-bath correlation functions.

title: Effect of Pb Substitution at the Mo site on the Magnetic Properties of the Polar Magnet Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, accepted by IEEE Transactions on Magnetics
summary: The ternary transition-metal oxide Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ is a polar magnet characterized by a layered structure of magnetic Fe honeycomb lattices and non-magnetic Mo kagome lattices. Whereas previous studies have primarily focused on the chemical substitution at the Fe sites to modulate the magnetic properties, the Mo sites have remained largely unexplored due to the strong spin-singlet trimerization of Mo$^{4+}$ ions. In this study, we investigated the effect of substituting non-magnetic Pb$^{4+}$ and Zr$^{4+}$ ions into the Mo sites to intentionally disrupt the Mo trimers. Our results reveal that the disruption of the Mo spin-singlet state induces active spins within the Mo layer, resulting in the emergence of a ferromagnetic-like behavior that persists even at room temperature. Quantitative analysis that takes into account the weight fraction of the main phase suggests an effective spin $S = 1/2$ state per active Mo ion upon trimer disruption. These findings demonstrate that controlling non-magnetic cluster states within a polar host via chemical substitution is a promising approach for designing room-temperature magnetoelectric materials.

AI.tldr: Substituting non-magnetic Pb⁴⁺ and Zr⁴⁺ into Mo sites of Fe₂Mo₃O₈ disrupts Mo spin-singlet trimers, inducing active Mo spins that produce room-temperature ferromagnetic-like behavior with effective S=1/2 per Mo ion.
AI.motivation: Previous studies focused on chemical substitution at Fe sites to modulate magnetic properties, while Mo sites remained unexplored due to strong spin-singlet trimerization of Mo⁴⁺ ions.
AI.method: Substituting non-magnetic Pb⁴⁺ and Zr⁴⁺ into Mo sites of the polar magnet Fe₂Mo₃O₈ to intentionally disrupt Mo trimers, followed by quantitative magnetic analysis considering main phase weight fraction.
AI.result: Disruption of Mo spin-singlet state induces active spins in the Mo layer, leading to ferromagnetic-like behavior persisting at room temperature, with an effective S=1/2 per active Mo ion.
AI.conclusion: Controlling non-magnetic cluster states within a polar host via chemical substitution is a promising approach for designing room-temperature magnetoelectric materials.

title: Microwave-Stimulated Serpentinization of Olivine for Geological Hydrogen Production
summary: Serpentinization of ultramafic rocks is a naturally occurring mineralogical process that can generate molecular hydrogen through the oxidation of ferrous iron during water-rock reaction. Although the resource potential is large, the natural reaction is kinetically limited, and practical hydrogen recovery requires methods that can accelerate conversion without imposing an energy penalty that exceeds the value of the hydrogen produced. This short communication reports a preliminary atmospheric-pressure microwave serpentinization experiment using a water-saturated 2 g crushed olivine sample. Microwave irradiation produced a rapid increase in measured hydrogen concentration compared with conventional hot-plate heating under otherwise similar conditions. The preliminary experiment showed approximately a 12-fold increase in hydrogen concentration and an apparent rate increase from about 2 ppb s$^{-1}$ for conventional heating to about 10 ppb s$^{-1}$ during microwave exposure. These results suggest that electromagnetic stimulation can enhance serpentinization kinetics, likely through rapid volumetric heating, selective coupling to iron-bearing phases, and localized thermal gradients. The result provides an initial experimental basis for evaluating microwave stimulation as a route to accelerated geologic hydrogen production and motivates follow-on measurements using calibrated gas analysis, absorbed-power measurements, dielectric characterization, and elevated-pressure testing.

AI.tldr: Microwave irradiation of water-saturated olivine accelerates serpentinization, boosting H₂ concentration ~12× and rate from ~2 to ~10 ppb/s compared to conventional heating, suggesting electromagnetic stimulation could enable kinetically enhanced geologic hydrogen production.
AI.motivation: Serpentinization can generate molecular hydrogen (H₂) naturally, but the reaction is kinetically limited. Practical H₂ recovery requires acceleration methods that don't incur an energy penalty negating the hydrogen's value.
AI.method: Atmospheric-pressure microwave serpentinization experiment using a water-saturated 2 g crushed olivine sample. Measured H₂ concentration compared with conventional hot-plate heating under similar conditions.
AI.result: ~12-fold increase in H₂ concentration; apparent rate increase from ~2 ppb/s (conventional) to ~10 ppb/s (microwave).
AI.conclusion: Electromagnetic stimulation can enhance serpentinization kinetics via rapid volumetric heating, selective coupling to iron-bearing phases, and localized thermal gradients. Provides initial experimental basis for microwave stimulation as a route to accelerated geologic H₂ production, motivating follow-up measurements.

title: Two-dimensional alternating ferrimagnetism with strain-controlled half-metallic state and valley polarization
summary: The discovery of altermagnetism offers new opportunities for exploring novel quantum states and developing spintronic devices for enabling momentum dependent spin splitting in compensated systems, while zero net magnetization limit its manipulability using conventional magnetic method. Here, we propose 2D alternating ferrimagnetism,a phase merging alternating momentum dependent spin splitting with a finite net magnetization. A tight binding model reveals that alternating ferrimagnetism originates from uncompensated magnetization in altermagnets, facilitating concurrent net magnetization and alternating spin splitting. First principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate stable alternating ferrimagnetism in strained and Cr substiting V2Te2O, which exhibit strain tunable net magnetization, reversable half metallicity and valley polarization, accompanied by long range magnetic order above room temperature. By combining altermagnetic and ferromagnetic properties, alternating ferrimagnetism expand the 2D magnetism landscape and offer pathways for energy efficient spintronic applications.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a new 2D magnetic phase called "alternating ferrimagnetism" that combines altermagnetic momentum-dependent spin splitting with finite net magnetization, demonstrated in strained Cr-substituted V2Te2O with room-temperature magnetic order and strain-tunable properties for spintronic applications.
AI.motivation: Altermagnetism offers momentum-dependent spin splitting in compensated (zero net magnetization) systems, but the lack of net magnetization limits control using conventional magnetic methods. The authors aim to create a phase that preserves alternating spin splitting while also having finite net magnetization for better manipulability.
AI.method: The authors use a tight-binding model to describe the origin of alternating ferrimagnetism from uncompensated magnetization in altermagnets. They then employ first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations to demonstrate stable alternating ferrimagnetism in strained and Cr-substituted V2Te2O.
AI.result: Strained and Cr-substituted V2Te2O exhibits alternating ferrimagnetism with strain-tunable net magnetization, reversible half-metallicity, valley polarization, and long-range magnetic order above room temperature.
AI.conclusion: Alternating ferrimagnetism expands the 2D magnetism landscape by merging altermagnetic and ferromagnetic properties, offering new pathways for energy-efficient spintronic applications and devices.

title: Entanglement Dynamics across a Monitored Quantum Point Contact
summary: We compute the entanglement dynamics across a monitored quantum point contact, where particle losses are recorded on a given site, and demonstrate how this single-site local monitoring substantially reshapes the entanglement production. Contrary to the unitary case, where entanglement entropy grows logarithmically in time, here we find first a linear growth, up to a maximum value displaying volume-law scaling, and then a slow decay to zero, as the system empties out. We capture this crossover using a quasiparticle picture, where the first linear growth arises due to an emergent bias voltage established by the losses, which eventually decays away as the system depletes. We connect our results to studies of the Page curve and to experimentally relevant probes, via full counting statistics of charge transfer across a subregion, with only a single channel to unravel leading to a favorable scaling of the postselection overhead. Natural platforms for this setting include mesoscopic systems and ultracold atoms.

AI.tldr: Monitoring a single-site quantum point contact with particle losses causes entanglement entropy to first grow linearly with volume-law scaling, then slowly decay to zero, contrasting with the unitary logarithmic growth.
AI.motivation: To understand how local monitoring (single-site particle losses) reshapes entanglement dynamics compared to unitary evolution, and to connect this to the Page curve and experimentally accessible measurements.
AI.method: The authors compute entanglement dynamics across a monitored quantum point contact with particle losses recorded on a single site, and develop a quasiparticle picture explaining the crossover from linear growth to decay via an emergent bias voltage established by losses.
AI.result: Entanglement entropy exhibits linear growth up to a volume-law maximum, then slow decay to zero. The crossover is captured by a quasiparticle model where an emergent bias voltage drives linear growth and then depletes.
AI.conclusion: Single-site local monitoring fundamentally alters entanglement production; the findings connect to Page curve studies and are testable in mesoscopic systems and ultracold atom platforms via full counting statistics with favorable postselection overhead.

title: Current-driven reduction of topological protection in multichannel superconductors
summary: We investigate the robustness of topological phases in a Kitaev ladder composed of two coupled superconducting chains under the perturbing influence of a finite charge current. By introducing an effective Hamiltonian depending on the quasiparticle momentum induced by the current, we show that the two-mode topological phase, present in the isolated ladder, is fragile against a finite current flux. To characterize this behavior, we combine bulk topological invariants with real-space diagnostics, including the edge-edge quantum conditional mutual information Iee, which provides an entanglement-based signature of topological order. Our results provide an effective framework to describe how current injection and measurement processes can affect topological protection in superconducting nanostructures.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how a finite charge current disrupts the topological phase in a Kitaev ladder (two coupled superconducting chains), using bulk topological invariants and entanglement-based measures like edge-edge quantum conditional mutual information to characterize the fragility of topological protection under current flow.
AI.motivation: To understand how topological phases in superconducting nanostructures behave under realistic current injection and measurement conditions, specifically testing the robustness of two-mode topological order in Kitaev ladders against finite current perturbations.
AI.method: Introduces an effective Hamiltonian dependent on quasiparticle momentum induced by the current; combines bulk topological invariants with real-space diagnostics, particularly the edge-edge quantum conditional mutual information (Iee) as an entanglement-based topological order signature.
AI.result: The two-mode topological phase present in the isolated Kitaev ladder is fragile and gets destroyed under a finite current flux.
AI.conclusion: Current injection and measurement processes can significantly affect topological protection in superconducting nanostructures, and the proposed framework combining topological invariants with entanglement measures effectively captures this behavior.

title: Nonlinear frequency shift and bistability of magnon-polarons
summary: We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of strongly coupled surface acoustic waves (SAWs) and spin waves (SWs) in a magnetoacoustic resonator based on a YIG/ZnO heterostructure by combining microwave reflection measurements with microfocused Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy. In the linear regime, the electrical response reveals clear hybridization between standing SAW cavity modes and finite-wave-vector SWs, resulting in pronounced avoided crossings. At elevated drive powers, the hybrid system exhibits a strongly field-dependent nonlinear response characterized by a positive frequency shift of the driven SW mode. Using the vector Hamiltonian formalism for nonlinear spin-wave dynamics, we show that this shift is dominated by a cross-shift term. In our resonator geometry, this contribution becomes significant because the standing SAW cavity mode simultaneously excites counterpropagating SWs with wave vectors $+k$ and $-k$. For suitable field detuning, the nonlinear shift drives the SW mode into resonance with the SAW excitation, leading to a strong enhancement of the magnon population, broadband nonlinear scattering, and bistable foldover behavior. Beyond the foldover threshold, both the magnon and phonon responses stabilize. These results establish SAW-driven $k \neq 0$ magnon-phonon hybrids as a promising platform for nonlinear magnetoacoustics and wave-based information processing.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates strongly coupled SAW-SW hybrids in a YIG/ZnO resonator, finding that cross-shift nonlinearity from counterpropagating SWs leads to resonance enhancement, bistable foldover, and stabilization, establishing a platform for nonlinear magnetoacoustics.
AI.motivation: To understand the nonlinear dynamics of strongly coupled surface acoustic waves (SAWs) and spin waves (SWs) in a magnetoacoustic resonator, and to explore their potential for wave-based information processing.
AI.method: Combined microwave reflection measurements with microfocused Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy on a YIG/ZnO heterostructure; used vector Hamiltonian formalism for nonlinear spin-wave dynamics to analyze the nonlinear shift.
AI.result: Observed clear hybridization with avoided crossings in linear regime; field-dependent nonlinear response with positive frequency shift dominated by a cross-shift term; beyond foldover threshold, both magnon and phonon responses stabilize.
AI.conclusion: SAW-driven k ≠ 0 magnon-phonon hybrids offer a promising platform for nonlinear magnetoacoustics and wave-based information processing.

title: Equilibrium Stabilization of a Hidden Phase Like Metallic State in 1T-TaS2
summary: Electronic phases that lie outside the equilibrium ground state offer a route to explore competing configurations in correlated materials. In 1T-TaS2, ultrafast excitation accesses a metallic hidden phase that is distinct from the commensurate insulating ground state. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to show that an equivalent electronic configuration is stabilized in exfoliated intermediate-thickness 1T-TaS2 flakes, where it persists up to room temperature before evolving through a different sequence of electronic transitions. This equilibrium hidden-phase-like state hosts a metallic band with finite Fermi-level spectral weight while retaining the characteristic hybridization gaps associated with the star-of-David band folding. These results establish a platform for controlling competing electronic states in layered materials, with implications for both quantum science and phase change technologies.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that a hidden metallic phase normally accessed only by ultrafast laser excitation in 1T-TaS2 can instead be stabilized at equilibrium in exfoliated intermediate-thickness flakes, where it persists up to room temperature and exhibits a distinct sequence of electronic transitions.
AI.motivation: To explore and stabilize electronic phases outside the equilibrium ground state in correlated materials, specifically investigating whether the hidden metallic phase in 1T-TaS2 can exist at equilibrium without requiring ultrafast excitation.
AI.method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) performed on exfoliated intermediate-thickness 1T-TaS2 flakes to characterize the electronic structure of the equilibrium hidden-phase-like state.
AI.result: An equilibrium hidden-phase-like state was found in exfoliated intermediate-thickness 1T-TaS2 flakes, which persists up to room temperature. This state hosts a metallic band with finite Fermi-level spectral weight while retaining characteristic hybridization gaps associated with star-of-David band folding.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a platform for controlling competing electronic states in layered materials, with implications for quantum science and phase change technologies.

title: Optical anisotropy and electronic states in the pleochroic material Ca$_3$ReO$_5$Cl$_2$
summary: Pleochroism is a type of optical anisotropy in which the apparent color of a material varies depending on the polarization and propagation direction of incident light. The oxychloride compound Ca$_3$ReO$_5$Cl$_2$ has recently attracted attention due to its pronounced pleochroism. The paramagnetic state of this compound, characterized by localized Re 5$d$ electrons, is challenging to describe within conventional first-principles methods. In this study, we investigate the optical anisotropy in Ca$_3$ReO$_5$Cl$_2$ using first-principles calculations, with particular focus on the relationship between the optical spectra and electronic states. We employ a ferromagnetically ordered state to effectively capture the localized character of the Re 5$d$ electrons. The calculated dielectric function and absorption coefficient qualitatively reproduce the experimentally observed peak structures. An orbital-resolved analysis indicates that the characteristic optical transitions associated with the pleochroism predominantly involve Re-$d$-dominated electronic states, highlighting the key role of the Re $d$ electrons in the pleochroic optical response of Ca$_3$ReO$_5$Cl$_2$.

AI.tldr: The study uses first-principles calculations with a ferromagnetic ordered state to investigate the pronounced pleochroism (optical anisotropy) in Ca₃ReO₅Cl₂, finding that the characteristic optical transitions predominantly involve Re 5d electrons, which explains the experimentally observed pleochroic behavior.
AI.motivation: The paramagnetic state of Ca₃ReO₅Cl₂, characterized by localized Re 5d electrons, is challenging to describe within conventional first-principles methods, motivating the need for an alternative computational approach to understand the pronounced pleochroism observed in this material.
AI.method: First-principles calculations are performed using a ferromagnetically ordered state to capture the localized character of Re 5d electrons, with orbital-resolved analysis of the dielectric function and absorption coefficient.
AI.result: The calculated dielectric function and absorption coefficient qualitatively reproduce experimentally observed peak structures. Orbital-resolved analysis shows that the pleochroic optical transitions predominantly involve Re-d-dominated electronic states.
AI.conclusion: Re 5d electrons play a key role in the pleochroic optical response of Ca₃ReO₅Cl₂, and the ferromagnetic ordering approach effectively captures the localized electronic character needed to describe this optical anisotropy.

title: Topological semimetals: surface transport and spin effects
summary: For the solid state physics, recent interest to topological systems is mostly connected with topological semimetals, in particular, to Weyl ones as the most representative semimetal type. Like other topological materials, e.g. topological and Chern insulators, topological semimetals acquire topologically protected surface states with linear dispersion. In contrast to helical surface states in topological insulators, the surface states are chiral for Weyl semimetals, similarly to Chern insulators, which allows to consider Weyl semimetals as the three-dimensional analog of the quantum Hall effect regime. Weyl semimetals are also interesting for spin-dependent effects, due to the spin-momentum locking in the topological surface states. For topological semimetals, the main problem of transport investigations is to reveal the surface states contribution in the material with gapless bulk spectrum. Here, we present review of experimental results on charge and spin transport in topological semimetals: charge transport in different superconducting proximity devices; spin-dependent transport; magnetic response of the topological surface states; non-linear anomalous Hall effect as the direct manifestation of the non-zero Berry curvature in topological semimetals. Possible applications are also considered for this new class of topological materials.

AI.tldr: This review examines charge and spin transport in topological semimetals, focusing on Weyl semimetals as 3D analogs of the quantum Hall effect, including superconducting proximity devices, spin-dependent transport, magnetic response of surface states, and nonlinear anomalous Hall effects as manifestations of Berry curvature.
AI.motivation: The main problem in transport investigations of topological semimetals is revealing surface state contributions in materials with gapless bulk spectra, motivating the need for a comprehensive review of experimental results on charge and spin transport.
AI.method: Review of experimental results on charge transport in superconducting proximity devices, spin-dependent transport, magnetic response of topological surface states, and nonlinear anomalous Hall effects indicative of nonzero Berry curvature.
AI.result: Topological semimetals exhibit chiral surface states with spin-momentum locking; nonlinear anomalous Hall effect directly manifests nonzero Berry curvature; surface state contributions can be isolated despite gapless bulk spectra.
AI.conclusion: Weyl semimetals represent a new class of topological materials with potential applications in spin-dependent transport and as three-dimensional analogs of the quantum Hall effect regime.

title: Topologically Driven Giant Effective Spin Mixing Conductance in Antiferromagnetic FeSn/Py Heterostructures
summary: The topological semimetal FeSn antiferromagnet, characterized by its kagome lattice, two-dimensional flat bands, and Dirac-like surface states, holds immense promise for spintronic applications. In this work, for the first time, we investigate the spin pumping behavior in epitaxial-FeSn/Py (Ni$_{80}$Fe$_{20}$) heterostructures. We report a giant effective spin mixing conductance (g$^{\uparrow \downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}}$) of $(116\pm 7)$~nm$^{-2}$, which is nearly one order of magnitude higher than that of standard Pt/Py heterostructures. The insertion of a 3 nm Al spacer layer results in a two-fold reduction in the effective damping, confirming the interfacial origin of the large g$^{\uparrow\downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}}$. Consistently, we observe an order-of-magnitude higher inverse spin Hall effect voltage in the FeSn/Py system compared to a reference Pt/Py film stack. We attribute the giant g$^{\uparrow\downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ to the direct interfacing of the Py layer with the topologically active [001]-kagome surface of epitaxial-FeSn. These findings establish the critical role of topologically active interfaces for advanced quantum-material-based spintronic devices.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first investigation of spin pumping in epitaxial-FeSn/Py heterostructures, revealing a giant effective spin mixing conductance (~116 nm⁻²) that is an order of magnitude higher than standard Pt/Py systems, attributed to the topological [001]-kagome surface of FeSn, with potential implications for quantum-material-based spintronics.
AI.motivation: To explore the spin pumping behavior in FeSn/Py heterostructures for the first time, leveraging FeSn's topological semimetal properties (kagome lattice, flat bands, Dirac surface states) for enhanced spintronic performance.
AI.method: Spin pumping measurements in epitaxial-FeSn/Py heterostructures with and without Al spacer layers; comparison to reference Pt/Py systems; analysis of effective damping and inverse spin Hall effect voltage.
AI.result: Giant effective spin mixing conductance of (116±7) nm⁻², nearly 10× higher than Pt/Py; Al spacer reduces effective damping by two-fold; inverse spin Hall voltage one order of magnitude higher than Pt/Py reference.
AI.conclusion: The giant spin mixing conductance originates from direct interfacing of Py with the topologically active [001]-kagome surface of epitaxial-FeSn, establishing the importance of topologically active interfaces for advanced spintronic devices.

title: Emergent magnetic and charge ordered phases in freestanding ultrathin \ce{LaVO3}
summary: Transition metal oxide perovskites are an ideal platform for exploring the interplay between spin, orbital, charge and lattice degrees of freedom. Among them, \ce{LaVO3} has been extensively studied in heterostructures and superlattices, where exotic phases have been reported. Motivated by the advances in freestanding oxide membranes, we investigate the intrinsic properties of freestanding ultrathin \ce{LaVO3} films using density functional theory. Our calculations reveal a sequence of magnetic phase transitions with thickness, starting from stripe-AFM in monolayer until the bulk like C-AFM is recovered. Beyond four layers, polar catastrophe driven charge transfer dopes the surface layers giving rise to stripe-AFM and ferromagnetic surface states while the central layers remain bulk like. We further explore this fact by studying charge doped monolayer, discovering that hole doping drives the system into ferromagnetic state. Doping also induced charge ordering in the system. A striped charge ordering pattern is observed at 0.5 h/fu, while a 3:1 stripe pattern emerges at 0.25 h/fu, indicating that the periodicity of the superstructure changes with doping concentration.

AI.tldr: Using DFT calculations, the study reveals that freestanding LaVO₃ ultrathin films undergo thickness-dependent magnetic phase transitions from stripe-AFM to bulk-like C-AFM, with surface charge doping (driven by polar catastrophe) inducing ferromagnetic and stripe-AFM states, while hole doping in monolayers leads to ferromagnetism and doping-concentration-dependent charge ordering patterns.
AI.motivation: To investigate the intrinsic properties of freestanding ultrathin LaVO₃ films, motivated by advances in freestanding oxide membranes and the need to understand spin-orbital-charge-lattice coupling in transition metal oxide perovskites beyond substrate-constrained heterostructures.
AI.method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on freestanding ultrathin LaVO₃ films of varying thickness, supplemented by charge-doped monolayer studies.
AI.result: A sequence of magnetic phase transitions with thickness: stripe-AFM in monolayer → bulk-like C-AFM recovered beyond a few layers; beyond four layers, polar catastrophe-driven charge transfer dopes surface layers, creating stripe-AFM and ferromagnetic surface states while central layers remain bulk-like. Hole doping in monolayers induces ferromagnetism and charge ordering: striped charge ordering at 0.5 h/fu and 3:1 stripe pattern at 0.25 h/fu.
AI.conclusion: The intrinsic magnetic properties of freestanding LaVO₃ films are strongly thickness- and doping-dependent, with polar catastrophe and charge doping offering tunable routes to engineer magnetic and charge-ordered phases in oxide membranes.

title: First-Principles Study of Fe Adsorption and Its Effects on the Mechanical and Electrical Properties of Monolayer and Bilayer Biphenylene Networks
summary: Biphenylene network (BPN) is a 2D carbon allotrope that exhibits promising potential for applications. In this work, we systematically investigated the adsorption characteristics of Fe atoms on monolayer and bilayer BPN. Structural optimization and adsorption energy analysis reveal that, for monolayer BPN, the average adsorption gradually enhances with increasing Fe coverage, indicating a strengthening of Fe-substrate interactions. The most stable configuration is identified at an Fe/C ratio of 50 %. For bilayer BPN, the energetically preferred adsorption site for Fe atom is located at the center of the interlayer four-membered ring, with an average adsorption energy of -4.3 eV. Mechanical properties are further evaluated for pristine and Fe-decorated BPN. The results demonstrate that monolayer and bilayer BPN possess relatively high in-plane Young's and shear moduli, indicative of excellent in-plane mechanical stability. Fe adsorption is found to have only a minor effect on the in-plane mechanical properties of both monolayer and bilayer BPN, suggesting that the in-plane stiffness is predominantly governed by the intrinsic carbon framework. In contrast, the out-of-plane mechanical response of bilayer BPN is significantly affected by Fe incorporation. The effective out-of-plane elastic constant C33 of pristine bilayer BPN is calculated to be 24.59 GPa, indicating relatively weak interlayer interactions and facile deformation along the out-of-plane direction. Notably, this property can be substantially enhanced by interlayer Fe adsorption, with C33 increasing dramatically to 515.63 GPa upon an Fe/C ratio of 25 %.
